drafted_from: tool:make-a-picture-vector-set-of-my-videos's own row and meaning/test/meaning-search.test.mjs, whose builder run on synthetic videos answered the values shown here
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make a picture vector set of the videos in ~/Footage/card/CLIP into ~/Footage/picture-set, so I can find moments by what they show." It runs the builder on this computer and answers how many frames it kept.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads a folder of videos and writes a vector set folder on this computer.
instructions: 1. Name the folder of videos (input) and the folder for the set (output); the same output folder again adds only new videos.

2. Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:make-a-picture-vector-set-of-my-videos"} and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/search-everything-with-one-question/meaning/do-work/make_picture_vector_set.py --videos {input} --out {output}.
3. Read the last line {"result": {"frames", "added", "videos_done", "out"}}; output/vector-set.json holds the vector_set member for the index descriptor.

4. Search the set by what the pictures show with tool:search-everything-with-one-question; words are turned into the same kind of vector by tool:words-as-picture-vector, handed in to the search as query_vectors.

worked_examples.title: Two takes become five timed frames, and a second run adds nothing
worked_examples.ask: Make my two takes searchable by what they show.
worked_examples.given: From meaning/test/meaning-search.test.mjs: red-take.mp4 (6 s) and blue-take.mp4 (4 s), one frame every 2 s, with a smaller proxy copy of blue-take decoded instead.
worked_examples.hands_back: It printed result.frames 5 and wrote frames.jsonl rows blue-take.mp4 at 0 and 2 and red-take.mp4 at 0, 2 and 4; the same run again printed result.added 0.
